name: Basilica of Saint Mary of the Immaculate Conception, Norfolk
history: The parish began in 1791 as St. Patrick's, founded by French Catholics fleeing the French Revolution together with early Irish immigrants; it is the oldest parish in the Diocese of Richmond. Its 1842 church burned in 1856. The present church was completed in 1858 and rededicated to the Immaculate Conception, the dogma proclaimed in 1854. Today it is a historically Black Catholic parish.
arch: A stuccoed brick Gothic Revival church with a central three-stage tower and spire. It was listed on the National Register of Historic Places in 1979.
features: It is the only minor basilica in Virginia.
A $6.7 million restoration, finished in December 2020, also brought back the historic organ, silent since 1981.

look.d: The tall three-stage tower and spire is a downtown Norfolk landmark.
Locals call it "the Mother Church of Tidewater Virginia".

fun: Immaculate Conception in Towson, Maryland, was built from the same plans, but with a rose window instead of a spire.
journal: Founded by refugees in 1791. Now the only basilica in Virginia, and proudly Black Catholic.

quiz.q: What makes it unique in Virginia?
a: It is the state's only minor basilica
